gap: None of the results ChatGPT got says that BLUETTI's own US store sells the Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh, '10ms UPS Backup') at the same $499 as the AC180 that ChatGPT showed as a card, whose switchover BLUETTI states as 20 ms. So at the same price, one station switches over in half the time the other does.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Bambu forum thread 'Power Interruption Alert! Which UPS for a P1S+AMS?', the 'My Experience with a P1S Mid-Print Unexpected Utility Power Loss' thread, the P1S tech-spec and quick-start PDFs, and our current page. ChatGPT's own answer gives the AC180's 20 ms. In the forum thread, Heisenberg says a 20 ms transfer 'still does not interrupt the print', but that is an assumption nobody tested. None of these pages names a same-price station with a 10 ms spec. Our current page lists the AC180 at 20 ms but does not list the Elite 100 V2 at all. None of them turns the CyberPower's 'minutes at half load' figure into delivered Wh, so a 1500 VA UPS can't be compared with a 1 kWh power station. None notes that EcoFlow and Jackery give their older or bigger models 20–30 ms 'EPS' or 'switchover' times and their newer ones 10 ms.
decides: For keeping a P1S printing through a flicker, switchover time is the spec that matters, and a shorter one gives more margin. A 1 kWh station at $499 is now available from BLUETTI with a 10 ms rating (Elite 100 V2) instead of 20 ms (AC180). That makes the Elite 100 V2 the better 1 kWh pick at the same price. The AC180 drops to second place, because it has 128 Wh more capacity but a switchover twice as long. The CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD (4 ms typical) is still the safest pick for flickers only. Its vendor figures work out to about 83 Wh delivered at 500 W, roughly a twelfth of a 1 kWh station, so it is not a choice for riding out an outage. No published test shows a P1S rebooting on a 20 ms transfer, so the page should present this as spec margin, not as proven failure.

findings.label: UPS switchover, cycle life, warranty (maker page)
findings.value: 'automatically switches over in just 20ms during a power outage'; '3,500+ Cycles to 80% Original Capacity'; 5-year warranty; 1,800 W continuous / 2,700 W surge; the page states no UPS bypass-power limit
findings.note: The AC180's 20 ms is twice the Elite 100 V2's 10 ms at the same $499. The AC180 has 1,152 Wh against 1,024 Wh, which is 128 Wh more, or about 0.7 h more at 150 W after an 85% usable-energy factor.

findings.label: UPS switchover and bypass limit
findings.value: '≤10ms Pro-Grade UPS Backup: Seamless switch with 980W bypass power'; 600 W rated / 1,500 W lifting; 'Over 3,000 cycles' (no % stated)
findings.note: Bundle with a 100 W panel, $489.99. The 980 W bypass is far above the 350 W P1S peak on 110 V, so in UPS mode the grid-powered printer is not limited by the 600 W inverter.

findings.label: Capacity, transfer time and runtime turned into delivered energy
findings.value: 1,500 VA / 1,000 W; 4 ms typical transfer; 10 min at half load, 2.5 min at full load, which is about 83 Wh delivered at 500 W and about 42 Wh at 1,000 W; sealed lead-acid, RB1290X2 pack; pure sine wave on battery
findings.note: Arithmetic: 500 W × 10/60 h = 83 Wh; 1,000 W × 2.5/60 h = 42 Wh. At 150 W, delivered energy would be higher than 83 Wh (lead-acid gives more at lighter loads), but CyberPower publishes no figure at that load. Compared with a ~1,000 Wh station at 85% usable (~870 Wh), the UPS holds roughly a tenth to a twelfth as much. This is the 'CPA' global SKU page. The US cyberpowersystems.com page returned HTTP 405.

findings.value: '10ms Auto-Switch' (DELTA 3 Max / Max Plus / Ultra Plus listings); DELTA 3 Plus solar bundle $919; '3000+ cycles' to '80% of its original capacity'; 5-year warranty
findings.note: The 10 ms figure is printed on the Max/Ultra Plus listings in the same storecheck search (https://us.ecoflow.com/products/ecoflow-delta-3-max-plus-portable-power-station-2048wh). The DELTA 3 Plus bundle text I read does not repeat it.

findings.note: On the same store, the Explorer 2000 v2 is listed as 'Switchover happens in under 20ms' and the Explorer 300 as '4,000+ charge cycles to 70% capacity'.
